themeDerivation.whyToolFailed: The design binds NO SLDS-named variables. Its variable collection is legacy Kampus product tokens (Primary/$kampus-color-purple-7, grays/gray-1, UI/Button). theme-match.mjs compares Figma token NAMES to --sl-* custom property names, so it found zero comparable tokens and could not rank any theme.

themeDerivation.confidence: Best by a clear margin and the only theme carrying the design's brand purple #643695 as --sl-brand-light-color-palette-purple-700. BUT absolute agreement is 0.364, NOT the 1.0 every other known pairing achieves.
themeDerivation.finding: THE DESIGN HAS DRIFTED FROM EVERY THEME. Its entire neutral ramp (#29292B, #444548, #6D6E73, #CECFD2, #DFE3E6) and its purple-1 (#F0ECF5) and orange (#DB7109) exist in NO theme in the repo. Only the brand purple and three greys survive. confirmedAtResume.honestStatement: The evidence for kampus is WEAK and is being recorded as weak. theme-match reports confident:false because the design binds a legacy Kampus Figma library's variable names, not SLDS names, so there is almost nothing for a name-to-name comparison to work with. kampus is chosen because it is the best of a bad set (4/11 on direct hex, next best 2/11), it uniquely carries the brand purple #643695, and the sibling run on the same file chose it too. This is NOT the 1.0 agreement the four known pairings achieve.

tagNamespacing.problem: A1 and this run both minted a left-toolbar from the SAME Figma component with DIFFERENT APIs. The conventions require a GUARDED customElements.define, so a collision does not throw - whichever module loads first wins and the other frame silently gets the wrong component wearing its own attribute names.
tagNamespacing.a1Mitigation: A1 namespaced only its toolbar, to sl-a1-kampus-left-toolbar. It left sl-kampus-app-header and sl-kampus-toc-sidebar unprefixed.
tagNamespacing.thisRunMitigation: Every tag, class and EVENT name this run mints is prefixed sl-bknp- / Bknp. Event names matter as much as tags because they share one GlobalEventHandlersEventMap.
tagNamespacing.findingAboutTheConvention: A guarded define is the right call for idempotent re-registration but it converts a cross-run name collision from a loud error into a silent mis-render. Nothing in the pipeline detects it: tsc is per-module, the harness render report only checks that a tag registered and has a box, and it WOULD have one - just the wrong component's. The batch needs a registry-collision check, or the pipeline needs to namespace tags by run automatically.

a1Overlap.question: Do two frames from one Figma file produce compatible component boundaries?
a1Overlap.answer: PARTIALLY - the vocabularies converged exactly, the architecture did not.

converged.ToolId: IDENTICAL. A1: 'contents'|'edit-content'|'assignments'|'notes'|'access-key'. Mine: the same five, same kebab-case. Independently derived from the same captions.
converged.HeaderActionId: IDENTICAL. A1 AppHeaderActionId and my BknpHeaderAction are both 'search'|'notifications'|'help'|'account'.
converged.componentSet: Both independently identified the same shared chrome: a purple app header, a 5-item left tool rail, and a breadcrumb+title masthead.

diverged.AppNavId: A1 has FOUR entries including 'my-page'; mine has THREE and treats 'My page' as a separate home affordance outside the nav list. A genuine disagreement about what the nav contains.
diverged.toolbarModelShape: A1 ToolbarModel {activeToolId?, badges?: Partial<Record<ToolId,number>>}; mine ToolRailModel {userPhotoUrl, userPhotoAlt, activeToolId, badges: BknpToolBadge[]}. A1 omits the user photo entirely and its Record<ToolId,number> CANNOT express the design's bare dot badge (a badge with no count). Mine can, via optional count.
diverged.headerApiStyle: A1's app-header takes SCALAR props (activeNavId, notificationCount as separate reflected @propertys). Mine takes ONE cohesive HeaderNavModel object. The conventions explicitly mandate the cohesive model, so A1 diverges from the conventions here and I follow them. This is the clearest case where the two runs could NOT share an implementation without one of them changing.
diverged.typeLocation: A1 centralises contracts in a shared models.ts; my decomposition co-locates each type with its owning component.
diverged.ScopedElementsMixin: A1 uses it on app-header; this run bans it outright.

theDecisiveDifference.what: ICONS. A1 hand-drew five inline <svg> glyphs for the toolbar, with a code comment noting the theme has no icons for them. This run omits all five and records them as discrepancies.
theDecisiveDifference.why it matters: This is not a style difference - it is a violation of the batch's explicit rule that invented artwork must never enter a pixel-compared region. A1's toolbar region is therefore not measurable: any fidelity score over it is partly scoring a drawing the pipeline made up. The two toolbars are not interchangeable at all, and the discrepancy is in A1's favour visually and against it scientifically.
theDecisiveDifference.secondOrderRisk: A1's hand-drawn version sits in a sibling folder and reads as established local practice. An implementer told to 'mirror a neighbour' would copy the violation. I had to warn each implementer explicitly not to.

a1Overlap.couldTheyShareAnImplementation: The left toolbar: yes in principle - identical ToolId vocabulary, and the model shapes are reconcilable (A1's Record would need to become an array to express the dot badge). The app header: no, not without one side changing, because scalar-props vs cohesive-model is a direct conventions conflict. The subchapter card: untested here - A1 built theory-card/exercise-card for feed items instead, so it never minted a subchapter card at all, which means the batch's most-anticipated shared unit was never actually shared.

sldsApiDiscoveries.sl-breadcrumbs: Takes plain <a> light-DOM children. Sets its own role=navigation + aria-label='Breadcrumb trail'. typeScaleFinding.what: No single --sl-text-new-* step pairs the font-size the design wants with the line-height it wants. header-nav needed 14/24 and had to take fontSize from body-md and lineHeight from body-lg. notes-panel needed 16/20 and had to take fontSize from body-lg and lineHeight from body-md.
typeScaleFinding.whyItMatters: This is not a missing token. The theme's type scale is STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from the design's - the design's size/line-height pairs are not points on the kampus ramp. Every implementer hits it and each invents its own cross-family pairing, so the resolution is unstable across agents. Two of five hit it here; a run with more text would hit it more.
typeScaleFinding.noGateCatchesIt: check-tokens passes - both longhands exist and resolve. Only the pixel diff would show it, and only if the fallback face were not already shifting metrics.

paletteReachability.question: How much of this design's palette can the kampus theme actually express?
paletteReachability.method: For each distinct colour the design uses (12 bound Figma variables + 2 measured from the reference PNG), resolved every kampus token through its full var() chain and took the nearest by Euclidean RGB distance.
paletteReachability.conclusion: EXACT COLOUR FIDELITY IS UNREACHABLE FOR THIS DESIGN BY CONSTRUCTION. Only 5 of 14 colours have a token; the other 9 sit between ramp steps, four of them by more than 20 units. This is the direct, measurable consequence of the 0.42 theme agreement recorded at Stage 1: the design was drawn against a legacy Kampus Figma library whose palette is not the SLDS kampus ramp. A pixel-fidelity score for this design is therefore bounded well below 100% no matter how good the implementation is, and the residual is a property of the design-theme pairing, not of the run. Any batch-level fidelity comparison that does not normalise for this will rank this design unfairly against designs drawn on SLDS tokens.

collapsedTokenFinding.what: --sl-label-md-fontSize and --sl-text-sm-fontSize LOOK like the 18px step and are declared as such, but resolve to 12px in the browser.
collapsedTokenFinding.mechanism: :root declares --sl-label-md-fontSize: var(--sl-label-md-fontSize-userGroup). --sl-label-md-fontSize-userGroup is declared ONLY under [data-user-group='early'|'developing'|'advanced'] and one `body` rule. Nothing sets that attribute, so at :root the substitution is invalid at computed-value time and the whole --sl-label-* family collapses.
collapsedTokenFinding.measured: getComputedStyle(document.body) on the live story: --sl-label-md-fontSize = 12px, --sl-text-sm-fontSize = 12px. Card titles were rendering at 12px/16px where the design wants 18/24.
collapsedTokenFinding.whyNoGateCaughtIt: check-tokens asks whether a token is DECLARED. This one is declared - it just resolves to nothing useful. A token existing is not a token resolving correctly, and only a live getComputedStyle distinguishes them.
collapsedTokenFinding.scopeOfTheProblem: Every --sl-{label,text,title,heading,display,caption}-*-{fontSize,lineHeight} token in kampus goes through the same -userGroup indirection. The entire older type-size namespace is unusable. Only --sl-text-new-* and --sl-typography-* carry flat values.
collapsedTokenFinding.fix: Card title moved to --sl-text-new-body-lg-* (16/24). No un-gated token resolves to 18px, so a 2px delta was accepted in place of a silent 6px one.

fontFamilyFinding.what: The ENTIRE --sl-text-new-*-fontFamily namespace in kampus names 'Open Sans' (with a space). No loaded @font-face has that family name. The Typekit sheet the theme loads registers the family as 'open-sans' (hyphenated), which only the OLDER --sl-*-fontFamily namespace names.
fontFamilyFinding.measured: Canvas text measurement in the live story, 18px, string 'Chapter 1 Vastaa kysymyksiin': 'Open Sans' = 218.5px, identical to a deliberately nonexistent family (218.5px) and to serif (218.5px). 'open-sans' = 247.4px. document.fonts lists 'open-sans 400 loaded' and 'open-sans 700 loaded'.
fontFamilyFinding.consequence: Every component that followed the manifest's own guidance and used --sl-text-new-*-fontFamily rendered the whole page in the browser's default SERIF. I had recorded this as an [ENV] 'Kampus ships no fonts.css' discrepancy and that was WRONG - the font loads fine, the theme just names it incorrectly in one of its two namespaces.
fontFamilyFinding.fix: All six font-family declarations swapped to the older namespace (--sl-text-fontFamily, --sl-heading-fontFamily, --sl-caption-fontFamily). Size, line-height and weight stay on --sl-text-new-* / --sl-typography-*, which are correct.
fontFamilyFinding.whyNoGateCaughtIt: check-tokens verifies the token resolves - it does, to the string 'Open Sans'. Nothing verifies that a font-family VALUE names a face that is actually registered. This is mechanically checkable (compare each family token against document.fonts) and currently is not checked.
fontFamilyFinding.generalLesson: kampus has two parallel token namespaces that disagree: the new one has correct sizes but a broken family name, the old one has a correct family name but sizes that collapse through -userGroup. Neither namespace is wholly usable; correct typography requires taking family from one and metrics from the other. No documentation says so.
